newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir car bomb kills two in high-security zone.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir car bomb kills two in high-security zone.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas detonated a car bomb on Wednesday in a tightly guarded zone of the capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state, killing at least two people and wounding five, authorities said.

The car, outfitted to resemble an official vehicle, exploded outside a high security building which houses more than 200 government officials and state lawmakers in the state's summer capital Srinagar, they said.
The vehicle had been driven beyond two check points to within 15 metres (50 feet) of the building, which escaped damage in the attack.
Two police drivers standing near the car died when it blew up at around 9 a.m. (0330 GMT), a senior police official said. Two policewomen were among the five wounded.
The Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen militant group claimed responsibility for the attack, saying it was their response to an ultimatum issued this week by the state's new chief minister, Farooq Abdullah.
Abdullah, who took office earlier this month after the first local elections in Jammu and Kashmir since a separatist revolt erupted in 1990, had ordered rebels to surrender their guns within 30 days.
"The bomb attack...by our Mujahideen is a reply to Farooq Abdullah and India's puppet government in Kashmir," Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen said in a statement.
The statement in Urdu was circulated to local newspaper offices in Srinagar.
Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen is fighting for the merger of the Himalayan state with neighbouring Pakistan.
The government released a statement which quoted Abdullah as urging lawmkers recently elected to the 87-member assembly to tighten up personal security.

"The chief minister made a fervent appeal to the member of the house to take all precautionary measures for their personal safety besides the security provided to them by the government, as militancy was not out as yet," the government statement said.

Abdullah said security would be tightened around the building housing the lawmakers, each of whom has been provided a bullet-proof car, two jeeps and a security entourage of a dozen paramilitary troopers.
It was the fourth blast since a new state government, led by the state's National Conference party, assumed office after last month's local assembly polls, the first in nine years.
Seven relatives of a campaign worker for the National Conference were killed in a blast on Monday, local news agencies reported.
Police and hospital sources say at least 20,000 people have been killed in more than six years of separatist violence in the region. Abdullah has said the toll is closer to 50,000.
Dozens of separatist groups have been fighting for independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan since the revolt broke out in 1990.
Mainly Moslem Kashmir has been the cause of two of the three wars between India and Pakistan since the two nations won independence from Britain in 1947.
